**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject batching pairwise diff mode**

When `--batch --diff a.png b.png` is used, parsing accepts the two required diff resources, but each batch child is rewritten to contain only one resource here. `run_diff` then indexes `cli.resources[1]` and panics instead of returning a controlled error; either reject this mode with `--batch` or preserve diff inputs as pairs.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Suppress child diagnostics in JSON batch reports**

When a batch item fails under `--report json`, forcing the child to `Human` makes it print a `rich: ...` diagnostic to stderr before the aggregate JSON object. Consumers expecting the documented single machine-readable envelope cannot parse that stream; collect or suppress child diagnostics rather than emitting them in human form.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve batch failure exit classes**

For batch items that fail with a data error such as malformed JSON, the underlying exit code is 4, but the aggregate is hard-coded to the input class and exit code 3. This defeats the stable exit-code contract for automation and likewise loses gate failures; derive the aggregate class from the actual child statuses rather than labeling every failure as input.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve export kinds instead of inferring extensions**

Batch exports disappear silently whenever the destination does not end in lowercase `.html` or `.svg`. For example, `--batch --export-html result.out file.md` plans `result.out`, then clears `export_html` here, exits successfully, and creates no file even though the existing option accepts any PATH; retain whether each planned path came from the HTML or SVG option.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Include on-disk collisions in suffix handling**

With `--collision suffix`, an already-existing destination bypasses this check because it only applies to the `Error` policy, while suffix generation only considered duplicates within the current plan. The subsequent export therefore overwrites the existing file without `--overwrite`; existing paths must participate in suffix selection as collisions.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Avoid following directory symlink cycles**

When a scanned directory contains a symlink to itself or an ancestor, `Path::is_dir()` follows the link and pushes it back onto the traversal stack indefinitely, producing ever-longer paths until resource exhaustion. Skip symlinked directories or track visited directory identities during recursive batch expansion.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Count only attempted batch items**

In fail-fast mode, if the first of several resources fails, `resources.len() - failures.len()` counts every unattempted resource as completed. The aggregate report can therefore claim that most of the plan completed when none succeeded; track attempted and successful items explicitly.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Honor subcommand modes over config defaults**

CLI-over-config precedence only recognizes mode flags, not the documented positional subcommands. With a config default such as `mode = "markdown"`, `rich json file.json` injects `--markdown` first, treats `json` as a resource, and fails with multiple resources instead of selecting JSON mode; include command aliases when detecting explicit CLI mode selection.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Match glob metacharacters instead of substrings**

Quoted patterns containing `?` are routed into the glob branch but never match because the literal `?` remains in the substring, while `*.md` matches any recursively discovered path merely containing `.md`, including names such as `file.md.bak`. Use actual simple-glob matching so the advertised patterns select the intended files.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Parse configuration as TOML**

Splitting every line at `#` corrupts valid TOML strings containing that character. For example, `export_html = "report#ci.html"` is silently interpreted as `report`, causing output to be written to the wrong path; use a TOML parser so quoting, comments, and escapes follow the advertised format.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Record binary-only conveniences in PORTING.md**

This adds project-specific batch and configuration behavior to the `rich` binary, but the commit leaves the `rich-cli` table in `docs/PORTING.md` unchanged. Add these conveniences to that porting map so future upstream syncs can distinguish intentional binary extensions from mirrored behavior, as required by the repository contract.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
